paragraphs.text: MCP Center for DeepSeek Harness: a sidebar panel + marketplace for MCP servers, with per-workspace/s
ession scope, auto or /command invocation, JSON import, and a model-facing mcp_manager tool. · DeepS
eek Harness 的 MCP 管理中心。
# dsh-mcp-center

> [!WARNING]
> **Personal local build — not published to npm, and not meant for anyone else to insta

ll.**
> This repository is used only to install the plugin into one local DeepSeek Harness profile
>

(a `link:` dependency pointing at this checkout). Nothing here is published to npm or to a
> mirror

, and it must not be installed from one.
>
> Why it matters: the `dsh-mcp-center-ui@0.2.0` on the re

gistry cannot boot DSH. Its client half
> registered the browser module as `dsh-mcp-center`, while t

he Host claims each bundle's boot-graph
> row by the package name `dsh-mcp-center-ui`; the row staye

d unregistered, the loader retried and
> executed the same file twice, threw `client-modules: duplic

ate factory registration`, and the Web
> GUI died with `Failed to load plugins` / `web boot: 1 entry

did not activate` (crash log:
> `~/Library/Logs/DeepSeek Harness/crash-*-web-boot.log`).
>
> That d

efect is fixed in `v0.2.1` in this repository only — it is **not** being pushed back to the
> regist

ry. If you already installed 0.2.0 (or installed this plugin from a registry/mirror), remove
> it fi
rst and use this source instead; do not hand 0.2.0 to others.
One page for every MCP server in DeepSeek Harness: browse a curated marketplace, add a server from a
manual form or a pasted `mcpServers` block, scope it to all sessions / a workspace / a session, and
choose automatic or slash-command invocation.
## What it does
- **Sidebar entry `mcp`** (order 40, after Plugins / Automations / Skills Center) that opens the MCP

Center page in the main column.
- **Three tabs**: *Configured* (status, command or URL, tool count,

scope, invocation mode, enable / edit / test / expand / delete), *Marketplace*, *Invoke*.
- **Marke
tplace** ships 19 curated real MCP servers plus one offline demo server: category filter, search, re
quirement badges (key / OAuth / Node / Python / uv / Docker / network), and a quick-add dialog gener

ated from each entry's `fields`.
- **Two ways to add a server**: a manual form (stdio or streamable-
http, command, args, env, URL, headers, timeout) and a JSON import that understands Claude Desktop /
Cursor `mcpServers`, VS Code `servers`, or a single `{command}` / `{url}` object — several servers

at once, with a preview before anything is created.
- **Scope** — all sessions, specific workspaces,
or specific sessions. Out of scope means those tools are not merely discouraged: they leave that se

ssion's tool list and are rejected at execution.
- **Invocation mode** — `auto` puts the tools in th
e model's tool list; `manual` hides them and keeps them reachable only through `/mcp call`, the Invo

ke console, or the `mcp_manager` tool.
- **Model-side control** — the `mcp_manager` tool (`list`, `t
ools`, `market`, `add`, `update`, `remove`, `toggle`, `test`, `call`) and the `/mcp` command, both d
riving the same Host operations as the page.
## Security and data
- **Loopback only.** The page talks to the Host over `/api/dsh-mcp-center` on the Web GUI's own port
. A non-loopback request is answered `403` unless the plugin config sets `allowRemote: true` and the

caller is a paired remote device.
- **Secrets stay in the Host.** `env` and `headers` values are ma
sked in every response (`••••`, or first 3 + `••••` + last 2 characters). The page never receives a

stored secret, and an untouched field is submitted empty and keeps its stored value.
- **`env:NAME`
indirection.** Instead of storing a token, set the value to `env:GITHUB_TOKEN`. The generated bundle
then contains a live `process.env.GITHUB_TOKEN` reference, and the secret never enters `state.json`

.
- **State on disk.** `$DSH_HOME/mcp-center/state.json` (`~/.dsh` by default) is written with mode
`0600`, because it can contain API keys. On Windows the effective permissions come from the director

y ACL, so treat the file as sensitive either way.
- **Full Host privileges.** This is an ordinary in
-process DSH plugin: it runs inside the Host with the same privileges as any other bundle row, can s
pawn the `stdio` processes you configure, and can read the environment the Host runs in. Only add se
rvers you trust, and read a marketplace entry's `command` before adding it.
Exact schema and rules: docs/configuration.md.
## Compatibility
| Requirement | Value |

| DSH runtime | `>=0.2.0-rc` (verified against 0.2.1-rc.5 / desktop app 44.7.0) |
| Node.js | `>=22`

(the Host's runtime starts `stdio` servers) |
| Browser | the Harness Web GUI; the Client half load

s at page start |
| External tools | `stdio` marketplace entries need `npx`, `uvx`, or `docker` on `
PATH`, plus network access on first run |
The MCP protocol is not implemented here: framing, handshakes, tool calls and resources are delegate
d to the shipped `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client`. This plugin only materializes configuration for it.
## Known limitations
- **Removing a stored secret from the panel is not wired up.** Clearing a key/value row in the edit
dialog keeps the stored value (`""` means "unchanged"). The Host API does accept a delete: `POST /ap
i/dsh-mcp-center/action` with `{"action":"update","id":"<server>","patch":{"env":{"KEY":null}}}`. Pr

efer `env:NAME` refs so the secret never lands in `state.json` at all.
- **Uninstall the plugin befo
re its generated bundles.** If `dsh-mcp-center` is removed while `@dsh-mcp-center/server-<id>` rows
are still installed, those servers keep loading through `@deepseek-ai/dsh-mcp-client` with no scope
or invocation-mode enforcement. Delete the servers first (Configured → delete), or remove the leftov

er rows from the Plugins page.
- **OAuth-only marketplace entries have no OAuth flow.** Notion and S
entry are listed for their tool surface but will answer `401` until you add a token-based server ins

tead; the GitHub and Linear entries use plain PAT headers.
- **`state.json` mode `0600` is exact on
POSIX and advisory on Windows**, where the file inherits the directory ACL. Treat the file as sensit

ive on every platform.
- **Adopted external servers report `streamable-http`** in the edit form even
when the real transport is `stdio`, because only the tool namespace is observable from the outside.
